The implementation is complete and thoroughly verified. Here's a summary of what I built:

## `/app/submission/main.py` (23,842 bytes, regular file, stdlib-only)

**Section 1 — Envelope validation:** strict JSON ingest (rejects BOM, malformed UTF-8, trailing data, `NaN`/`Infinity`, duplicate keys at any level via `object_pairs_hook`), exact key sets at every level, integer checks that exclude booleans/floats, ID grammar, aliases that must already be canonical + globally unique + never the anonymous URI, access/relay peer rules, `ttl_ms`/`capacity` ranges, event schema, nondecreasing `t`, relay-auth-null, and all size limits → exit **2** with empty stdout.

**Section 2 — URI language:** exactly-once percent decoding restricted to RFC 3261 unreserved, case-sensitive user, DNS-style host (label count/length, alnum edges, letter-initial TLD, no escapes/IP literals/underscores), port normalization without leading zeros, tel separator stripping with 3–15 digit / leading-nonzero constraints.

**Section 3 — Wire syntax:** first `\r\n\r\n` split, byte/line/count/size bounds, exact start line, token header names with compact normalization (`f/t/i/l`), folding joined with one SP, singleton enforcement, Content-Length matching, and full grammar for From (one address + exactly one `;tag=`), To (SIP/SIPS, equal to canonical target), Call-ID, CSeq, PAI/PPI (comma split outside quotes/brackets, 1–2 items, one SIP/SIPS + one tel, canonical ordering) and Privacy.

**Sections 4–6 — Policy, ledger, output:** access PPI/default selection with PAI discarding; relay PAI-only resolution with allow-lists; From alias-or-anonymous+`id`; From rewriting and external PAI stripping; TTL expiration before every event keyed on original insert time; 9-part semantic commitment; accept/replay/conflict with no refresh; capacity eviction by oldest insertion index; staged reasons `hex → syntax → headers → length → fields → auth → identity → conflict`.

**Verification:** public example passes; 92 staged-rejection cases; ~55 envelope valid/invalid cases; ledger TTL/capacity/conflict/eviction-order semantics; full privacy × egress × peer-mode projection matrix; ~200 URI/address/field unit cases; exact size boundaries (65536/32768/8192/256); a differential test against an independently written reference model of sections 4–6; a spelling-equivalence test proving folded/compact/percent-escaped/case-varied retransmissions yield `replay` (not `conflict`); mutation fuzzing (no crashes, schema-valid output); and performance (10,000 events / 16 MiB input in ~0.6 s, ~64 MiB RSS).
